paras: The police beating of Claude Cheeks was an incident in Chicago in late July or early August 1920 in which Cheeks, a 36-year-old South Side resident, suffered severe head injuries while in the hands of police. The Chicago Whip reported that he was beaten by several officers while under arrest, while the Chicago Defender carried the officers' version that he had fired on them and injured himself while fleeing.

Neither report gives the date of the incident; both appeared on August 7, 1920, in local-news columns whose other items are dated in the last days of July. According to the Whip, Cheeks, of 5204 South Dearborn Street, "was severely beaten while under arrest by several officers of the 48th St. Station sustaining severe injuries of the head." He was then removed to Provident Hospital. The Whip did not say why he had been arrested.

The Defender's item, which names officers Ward and Dellogo, said the two caught Cheeks "prowling in an alley at 4 a.m." In that account Cheeks opened fire, "emptying his gun at them," and while trying to escape struck his head against the Rock Island elevated structure at 45th Street and was knocked unconscious. The Defender's version, which follows the officers' side, attributes the injury to Cheeks himself and mentions no beating, and it places the officers in the "16 precinct" rather than the 48th St. Station.
No report of charges against Cheeks, a complaint against the officers, or any inquiry appears in the coverage.

Only Chicago's two Black weeklies reported the incident, each in a single paragraph of a column of local police and hospital news, without a headline of its own. The Whip stated the beating as fact among items on stabbings, family quarrels and accidents, without comment. The Defender, in a similar column, printed the arresting officers' account without attributing it to them or questioning it. No white-press coverage of the incident was found.

reader.title: Police beating of Claude Cheeks
bases: The Whip reports that Cheeks was beaten by several police officers while under arrest (A1); the Defender's version also centers on an encounter with two officers (A2).

Both papers report that Cheeks suffered a head injury in an encounter with police, but the Whip attributes it to a beating by officers (A1) while the Defender says he fired on officers and struck his head on an elevated structure while escaping (A2).

framing.detail: The Whip lists the case among routine police items but states plainly that Cheeks was 'severely beaten while under arrest by several officers', without comment.
The Defender relays the officers' version (prowling, firing on police, self-inflicted head injury) without attribution or comment, in a column of local news.
